transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-11 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Miles (Redwood AE), Avery Chen (Redwood SE), Taylor Ng (Redwood Solutions), Maya Rios (Cobaltix Procurement), Priya Shah (Cobaltix Legal), Leo Grant (Cobaltix Infosec), Owen Park (Cobaltix ML)

Summary (auto): agreed pilot + legal redline path, need SOW and benchmark data.

[00:00] Jordan Miles: okay uh thanks everyone for joining on time, um we'll kick off — this is Jordan from Redwood. Today the agenda is the M S A and D P A handover, SLA targets for pilot and longer term, and the pricing pathways.
[00:18] Maya Rios: hi all — from procurement side, quick ask is we need clear pricing buckets for both hosted and dedicated, also any egress fees called out.
[00:29] Avery Chen: sure, we'll walk through the pilot pricing and then a separate curve for reserved capacity. note, our math changes with batching and cache — sorry, kv cache behaviors.
[00:45] Priya Shah: hi, Priya from legal — we flagged two main DPA exceptions: subprocessors list and 3rd party logging. also need indemnity language clarified.
[00:57] Leo Grant: and infosec — K M S integrations matter to us; we need to know if you support customer-managed keys/H S M or only redwood-managed KMS.
[01:10] Jordan Miles: yes, good call. short answer: for Private deployments we support customer K M S; for Hosted we offer rekey + optional external K M S via partner flows, we'll confirm exact H S M providers in the doc. (murmur: might be confusing)
[01:36] Owen Park: quick technical — what's the expected p95/p99 for 1k rps inference with a 1024 token average?
[01:45] Avery Chen: rough ballpark for dedicated pods, p95 under 200ms for single-turn generative, p99 in the 300-400ms depending on model variant and quantization. with hosted shared it's higher, and we'd route by policy to cheaper variants. these are verified in our lab, we'll attach the benchmark csv.
[02:12] Maya Rios: okay we need that csv for procurement to model TCO. also any variable fees — egress, embedding units — call them out.
[02:25] Priya Shah: on the DPA, there's a clause about subprocessor notifications — we want 30 days notice and a right to object. is that negotiable?
[02:36] Jordan Miles: usual playbook is notification, but we can agree to 30 days for material new subprocessors and provide a narrow objection period. we'll mark that as a redline.
[02:49] Leo Grant: audit logs — retention and format? we want immutable logs for 12 months with export to our SIEM. does Redwood stream logs to customer V P C?
[03:02] Taylor Ng: yes, we offer streaming audit logs to customer endpoints, formats are JSON lines; retention configurable. default retention on hosted is 90 days unless enterprise add-on. will confirm export latency.
[03:22] Maya Rios: can you also specify costs for extended retention? budgeting needs numbers.
[03:29] Avery Chen: priced monthly per GB retained and per log stream; I don't have the exact number in my head, I'll include a pricing table in the S O W.
[03:40] Priya Shah: security questionnaires — we've got completed SOC2 docs but need evidence of ISO/27001? do you have that or roadmap?
[03:49] Jordan Miles: we are SOC 2 Type II in prod; ISO is on roadmap for Q4 but we'll give you the attestation and, if needed, a timeline.
[03:58] Owen Park: on private deployment — latency aside, what's the work to stand up a V P C private control plane? network peering steps?
[04:08] Avery Chen: typically it's a 2-3 week project: network peering, KMS handshake, routing, and we provide terraform modules. there are some customers that take longer depending on internal approvals.
[04:22] Maya Rios: any required firewall openings? our security team will want a list.
[04:27] Taylor Ng: yes we'll send a minimal port list and CIDR ranges. it's typically HTTPS + gRPC endpoints for the runtime, and a few healthcheck ports.
[04:40] Priya Shah: indemnity cap — our legal team wants a limitation aligned with fees, but also carveouts for willful misconduct. is that standard?
[04:51] Jordan Miles: we usually have a cap tied to 12 months of fees, with carveouts for gross negligence; I'll flag as negotiable but can propose standard language.
[05:05] Leo Grant: egress fees detail — are you charging for tokens leaving region or transferring to our S3?
[05:13] Avery Chen: egress is charged for outbound data transfer from hosted endpoints; for Private with peering it's usually waived but we'll outline when that applies. we'll add examples to make it concrete.
[05:28] Maya Rios: pilot scope — procurement needs a defined pilot cost, length, and success criteria. we prefer 4 weeks with clear latency, cost per 1k calls, and accuracy checks.
[05:39] Jordan Miles: agreed. propose 4 weeks, 100k calls budgeted, SLA target p95 < 250ms for dedicated baseline, and quality measured via customer prompt set with regression thresholds.
[05:52] Owen Park: on quality, we need eval harness and a way to replay prompts to measure regressions between rollouts. do you give a diff tool?
[06:01] Avery Chen: yes we have an evaluation suite and can run regressions on pinned model versions; we'll provide an exportsable csv of results and ROC-like metrics.
[06:12] Priya Shah: DPA-specific: data deletion and retention — can you guarantee deletion within X days and provide audit?
[06:22] Taylor Ng: we support data retention TTLs and retention policies, deletion events are logged; we'll include process and timing in the DPA appendix.
[06:33] Maya Rios: procurement will need price floor and price protections for the reserved capacity year.
[06:39] Jordan Miles: typical reserved commits come with a 12-month pricing protection on the committed units, and reserved discounts scale with volume. exceptions for cloud egress fees could apply. we'll spell out the contract period and waterfall.
[06:55] Leo Grant: network encryption in transit? TLS 1.2/1.3 okay? any mTLS support?
[07:03] Taylor Ng: TLS 1.3, and we do support mTLS for private deployments. we'll list cipher suites.
[07:14] Priya Shah: on subprocessor list — will you provide the full list or a limited set? and can we require notification before new ones?
[07:25] Jordan Miles: we'll provide the current list; for new ones we can add the 30 day notice clause and provide a mechanism to object.
[07:36] Maya Rios: ok on financials — is there a path to escrow or escrow-like assurances for key IP?
[07:44] Jordan Miles: we offer data escrow for model weights or critical configs in enterprise agreements; we'll add that as an optional line item.
[07:56] Owen Park: one more tech: can the KV cache be persisted across restarts in private? we'd like to warm the cache.
[08:04] Avery Chen: yes, persistent KV options exist for private and dedicated, with caveats around cache invalidation; we'll document expected warm-up times.
[08:18] [short crosstalk]
[08:30] Priya Shah: timeline — when can we expect the redlines back and the S O W?
[08:34] Jordan Miles: I'll circulate the redlined M S A and a draft S O W by 2025-07-15. Avery will add the runbook/benchmarks by 2025-07-18.
[08:45] Maya Rios: procurement wants a single sheet that shows 3 scenarios: pilot, 12-month reserved, and enterprise with private control plane including egress assumptions.
[08:56] Taylor Ng: we can do that — will include cost per 1k tokens, per embedding, and retention fees.
[09:07] Leo Grant: can we get a short architecture diagram for the private deployment showing where logs go and where keys live?
[09:14] Avery Chen: yes I'll attach a diagram and a minimal terraform snippet.
[09:21] Jordan Miles: great — any blockers to proceeding to pilot once legal signs off?
[09:25] Priya Shah: nothing major, just need DPA exceptions reviewed and indemnity cap language OK'd.
[09:31] Maya Rios: procurement needs the final cost sheet to approve the pilot spend.
[09:36] Jordan Miles: understood — next steps recap: I'll send docs, Avery sends runbook, Priya/Leo review security/legal, then procurement schedules decision meeting.
[09:46] [wrap up]
[09:52] Jordan Miles: thanks everyone — we'll follow up in the thread with links.

Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-hearings (e.g., "K V cache" written as letters, "S O W" spaced out), some speaker overlap. Links mentioned: pilot runbook (link to shared drive), benchmark csv (attached in follow-up), draft M S A redline (to be shared).

End of transcript.
